Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients with evidence for severe insulin resistance or a disorder associated with severe insulin resistance must meet all of the following criteria: - Suspected severe insulin resistance, or a disorder associated with severe insulin resistance, as evidenced by one or more of the following: - Hyperinsulinemia (i.e. fasting insulin >30microU/mL) - High insulin requirement (> 2 units per kg per day or > 200 units total per day) - Phenotypic features suggesting a defect in glucose/lipid metabolism: - Acanthosis nigricans - Lipodystrophy/abnormal fat distribution - Xanthomata - Fatty liver - Known or suspected mutations of the insulin receptor gene - Known or suspected autoantibodies to the insulin receptor
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has type 2 diabetes, but there is no specific mention of hyperinsulinemia, high insulin requirements, or mutations/autoantibodies related to insulin resistance in the provided data.
The patient is 58 years old, which is well above the age requirement of 6 months.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Ability of subject or Legally Authorized Representative (LAR) to understand and the willingness to sign a written informed consent document.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has provided written informed consent, meeting this criterion.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: History of diabetes or abnormal glucose tolerance
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has a documented history of type 2 diabetes, which is explicitly listed as an exclusion criterion.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Psychiatric or cognitive disorder that will, in the opinion of the investigators, limit the subject's ability to provide informed consent/assent, or to comply with study procedures
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: There is no mention of any psychiatric or cognitive disorders in the patient's profile.
The patient is male, so this criterion does not apply.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Any other abnormality that, in the opinion of the investigator, will increase risk to the subject from participation, or interfere with interpretation of study data
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has coronary artery disease and elevated liver enzymes, which could potentially interfere with the study, but it is not explicitly stated as a disqualifying factor in the provided data.

Recap: The patient does not meet the inclusion criteria due to insufficient information on severe insulin resistance. He is excluded from the trial due to his history of diabetes. Other health issues like coronary artery disease and elevated liver enzymes may also pose risks, but they are not explicitly listed as exclusion criteria.
